Lessons.Title: Decimal Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will make sense of tenths and hundredths in decimal notation.
Key idea: Decimal notation to hundredths represents the number of shaded hundredth parts of one fixed whole.
How to reason: Count fractional parts on the 10-by-10 unit model and express 78/100 as the decimal 0.78.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up:  Notice and Wonder: Shaded Grid	 (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1:  Shady Fractions	 (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as Each large square represents 1., The shaded part of this diagram represents 0.01 or “1 hundredth.”, The shaded parts of this diagram represent 0.10 or “10 hundredths.”, They also represent 0.1 or “1 tenth.”. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2:  Ways to Express a Number	 (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as Each large square represents 1., Decimal: 0.78, \(\frac{8}{10}\), \(\frac{55}{100}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
